# 2016 Philippine presidential election in Zamboanga Sibugay

The 2016 Philippine presidential and vice presidential elections in Zamboanga Sibugay were held on Monday, May 9, 2016, as part of the 2016 Philippine general election in which all 81 provinces, all 145 cities, and all 1,489 municipalities participated. Voters voted the president and the vice president separately.

}}Davao City mayor Rodrigo Duterte won the province of Zamboanga Siugay and defeated DILG Secretary Mar Roxas, Senator Grace Poe, Vice president Jejomar Binay, and Senator Miriam Defensor Santiago by a clear margin in the presidential race.
Camarines Sur representative Leni Robredo won and defeated Senators Alan Peter Cayetano, Bongbong Marcos, Francis Escudero, Antonio Trillanes, and Gregorio Honasan.
This is the only province in the Zamboanga Peninsula in which Duterte won where Del Norte went to Roxas and Del Sur went to Poe.
Electoral system
According to the Constitution of the Philippines, the elections are held every six years after 1992, on the second Monday of May. The incumbent president is term limited and ineligible for re-election. The incumbent vice president is eligible to run for re-election and may run for two consecutive terms. The plurality voting system is used to determine the winner: the candidate with the highest number of votes, whether or not one has a majority, wins the presidency. The vice presidential election is a separate election, is held on the same rules, and voters may split their ticket. Both winners will serve six-year terms commencing on the noon of June 30, 2016, and ending on the same day six years later.
